basis: The two submissions are semantically identical. Both flip exactly one condition flag on one instruction in engine.inc (`ret nz` -> `ret z`) at the same site, with no other change. Same fault site, same mechanism, same scope, identical resulting object code; Y's hunk only spans one extra context line because its comment wraps onto three lines. The sole difference is comment prose, and both comments state the same invariant (piece values are white-relative, black's negated). Y adds a cross-reference to a sibling routine ("same convention as kingPstSigned below"), which I weighed as a possible formal-methods tell — an author maintaining a spec of sign conventions would check that every eval term agrees with one global convention — but it reads just as naturally as ordinary code-review diligence (grep the neighbour, match its convention), while an author who had proved the property would plausibly write X's terse restatement instead. The signal is symmetric. Nothing else discriminates: neither diff adds a test, an assertion, a spec/proof fragment, a conformance-suite entry, nor generalises the invariant beyond the single site — both leave the codebase with the sign convention recorded only in a comment. If forced off "cannot tell" I would lean very weakly to Y on the cross-reference, but that is comment style, not process evidence, and I do not think it supports a call.
